question.leadin: The 1569 Union of Lublin joined this region with Lithuania, and it underwent three partitions before 1800.
question.text: Name this country, which was invaded by the Nazis on September 1, 1939 to start World War II. The Soviets invaded this country two weeks later.
question.clue: The thirteenth of Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points called for this country's independence, and one of its leaders led a shipyard strike that resulted in the founding of a trade union.

swap.leadin: The firing of Anna Walentynowicz triggered a strike that led to the creation of this group.
swap.text: Name this trade union that grew from the 21 MKS Demands developed at the Gdansk shipyards.
swap.clue: Partly inspired by the 1971 essay Theses on Hope and Hopelessness, this organization secured its seat in government in a free election held in 1990, which led to a successful implementation of "shock therapy."

question.text: This first chairman of Solidarity became the first directly-elected President of Poland in 1990 and won the 1983 Nobel Peace Prize.
question.clue: His wife, Danuta, claimed his Nobel Peace Prize for him in 1983.

swap.leadin: It was partitioned several times in the late 18th century.
swap.text: Name this region whose king Jan Sobieski III dispersed the Ottomans during the Second Siege of Vienna, which became a modern-day country with its capital at Warsaw.
swap.clue: In the middle ages, this nation was ruled by the Piast Dynasty, whose kings included Boleslaw the Brave and Casimir the Great.

question.text: The szlachta paralyzed this Polish-Lithuanian parliament with the liberum veto, which allowed singular noblemen to stop the legislative process.
question.clue: The szlachta class composed the majority of its Chamber of Deputies.

swap.leadin: Winged hussars from this polity charged to victory at battles such as Klushino and Kluzyn.
swap.text: Identify this polity formed following the Union of Lublin which dissolved following a series of partitions.
swap.clue: Monarchs agreed to the Henrician Articles and made individual commitments called the pacta conventa on becoming rulers of this country.

question.text: The Deluge began with this Cossack rebellion, in which the Zaporozhian Host rebelled against Polish-Lithuanian rule in Ukraine under its namesake leader.
question.clue: This confict's victorious leader avenged the failure ten years prior of Jakub Ostrzanin, thanks to the help of the Tatar cavalry.

swap.leadin: Vytautas the Great was one ruler of this country.
swap.text: Name this country which joined with its western neighbor in the 1569 Union of Lublin. In the 20th century, this Baltic state was the first to declare its independence from the Soviet Union.
swap.answerHtml: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (accept Republic of Lithuania or Lietuvos Respublika)
swap.clue: Algirdas's victory over the Golden Horde at the Battle of Blue Waters drove the greatest expansionary period of this polity, whose ruler Vytautus's involvement with the Samogitian uprisings and incessant warring with the Teutonic Knights helped prompt the Battle of Grunwald. For 15 points, identify this Grand Duchy which participated in the 1569 Union of Lublin.

question.leadin: William Wilkinson was brought in from England to manage one of the burgeoning iron works in the early 19th century in this region.
question.text: Identify this region that was secured by Prussia following a successful defense of Chotusitz (KHO-too-zits) in 1742 during the War of Austrian Succession, which ended with Maria Theresa losing it to Prussia.
question.clue: Frederick the Great's 1740 occupation of this region triggered the War of the Austrian Succession.

swap.leadin: This group participated in the Round Table Talks.
swap.text: Name this trade union formed at Lenin Shipyard in Gdansk in 1980. It opposed the Soviets and Communism and supported workers through social activism and civil resistance.

question.text: The Janissary Revolt of 1622 followed a disastrous defeat at Choczim against this country, a combined commonwealth of two modern-day states ruled by the Jagiellon dynasty, with which the Ottomans had fought the Moldavian Magnate Wars. They often fought over Tatar and Cossack raids.
question.clue: Ruled by a form of government created by the Nihili Novi act, its main political doctrine could be summed up as "The King reigns but does not govern"; that political system was called the Golden Liberty.

swap.text: This man was made First Secretary of Poland's Communist Party in 1981 with instructions to crush Solidarity, which he nearly did, though his befuddlement at Poland's economic stagnation throughout the 1980s opened the door to liberalization.
swap.clue: In 2008, the IPN put this man on trial brutal crackdown which entrenched him as dictator in 1982.

question.leadin: One source records how during a rebellion in this city, people who could not pronounce the shibboleth "lentil, wheel, grinds, mill" were executed.
question.text: Name this city whose German-speaking population revolted in 1312 under a wojt ("vooyt") named Albert. In 1320, Wladyslaw ("v'wa-DISS-wahf") the Elbow-High was crowned king of Poland in this former Polish capitals's Wawel ("VAH-vell") Cathedral.
question.clue: Casimir III ruled from this city, which eclipsed early royal centers like Plock ("p'wotsk") and Gniezno ("g'nee-EZ-naw") after the pagan king Jogaila was baptized in its cathedral so he could marry the saint Queen Jadwiga ("yahd-VEE-gah").

swap.leadin: This period began with a rebellion by the Cossack leader Bogdan Khmelnitsky.
swap.text: Identify this period which fell during the reign of King John II Casimir, which was marked by incursions into that man's country by Charles X of Sweden.
swap.clue: Key precipitating factors of this period include the increased power of the nobility due to Sarmatism and Golden Liberty system, and it saw secondary conflicts like the Second Northern War.

question.leadin: During this country's resistance to Russification, the Knygnesiai, or Book Smugglers, promoted its native language.
question.text: Identify this country that joined Poland in the Union of Lublin and whose capital is Vilnius.
question.clue: Another Grand Duke of this nation signed the Union of Krewo to marry Jadwiga of Anjou.

swap.text: After the picnic, democracy came about through one of these orderly discussions in 1989. The Hungarian version of these events were inspired by ones organized by Solidarity in Poland.
swap.clue: Walesa attended one version of these negotiations that occurred in several countries between the Communist regimes and the opposition. In Poland in 1989, these talks resulted in semi-free elections and a victory for Solidarity.

question.text: Before Walesa was elected, this Polish general briefly served as President of Poland after the office's restoration. As Prime Minister, this man initiated the Round Table Talks that resulted in free Polish elections.
question.clue: Before his presidency, he was struck with a case of photokeratitis, which is why he continuously wears sunglasses in public.

swap.leadin: Polish negotiators drew on earlier legal precedents for a 1466 treaty named for this city, which Frederick II of Brandenburg and Jan Jiskra ("yan YIS-kruh")had failed to mediate.
swap.text: Name this city on the Vistula whose "First Peace" followed the Battle of Grunwald ("GROON-valt"). Poland annexed Royal Prussia at this city's "Second Peace" after the Thirteen Years' War.
swap.answerHtml: Thorn (“torn”) [or Toruń; accept First or Second Peace of Thorn or Toruń]

question.leadin: This man argued that it is "better to have a friend than a slave" in his seminal Essay on Diplomacy, which he wrote under the pseudonym "Philhellene" ("feel-eh-LEN").
question.text: Name this man who founded the Historical and Literary Society in Paris. This man bought the Hotel Lambert, which lends its name to a faction of people led by this man that participated in the Great Emigration.

swap.leadin: Apocryphally, this dynasty came to power after the cruel Prince Popiel II ("POPE-yell the second") was imprisoned and eaten alive by rats and mice.
swap.text: Name this dynasty that succeeded the Popielid dynasty. A history by Gallus Anonymus claims that this dynasty was founded by a namesake wheelwright with an always-full cellar, an ancestor of Boleslaw ("bo-LESS-waff") the Brave.
swap.clue: The semi-legendary namesake of this dynasty was a wheelwright who was legendarily visited by two angels in disguise who blessed his cellar.
